edits.new_text: 1. An input device for a man-machine interface comprising: an upper board providing a first plastic based resistant film structure; and a lower board corresponding to said upper board and providing a second plastic based resistant film structure opposite to said first plastic based resistant film structure; wherein, said first and second plastic based resistant film structures are respectively composed of an ITO based conductive film, a printed silver conductor layer, a carbon layer, an insulation layer and an adhesive layer, and wherein the carbon layer is disposed to stabilize the printed silver conductor layer against dissociation of silver ions caused by variable temperature and humidity.

6. An input device for a man-machine interface comprising: an upper board providing a first glass based resistant film structure; and a lower board corresponding to said upper plate and providing a second glass based resistant film structure opposite to said first glass based resistant film structure; wherein, said first and second glass based resistant film structures are respectively composed of an ITO glass based conductive film, a printed silver conductor layer, a carbon layer, an insulation layer and an adhesive layer, and wherein the carbon layer is disposed to stabilize the printed silver conductor layer against dissociation of silver ions caused by variable temperature and humidity.

arguments.assertion: The cited reference (Aufderheide) as characterized in the Office action does not disclose a carbon layer that is expressly disclosed and claimed as being disposed to stabilize the printed silver conductor layer against dissociation of silver ions caused by variable temperature and humidity, which is a structural and functional limitation added to claims 1 and 6.
arguments.support_span: It is worth to mention that the carbon film layer, which is arranged in the plastic based resistant film structure 30 and the glass based resistant film structure 40, is capable of significantly stabilizing the electrons and restricting the phenomenon of the silver ions being possibly dissociated from the conductor layer resulting from the variable temperature and humidity.

arguments.assertion: Claims 4, 5, 9 and 10 recite particular layer orderings and the specification discloses both ordering alternatives and the carbon layer's stabilizing function; the Examiner's cited reference has not been shown to disclose the particular claimed combination including the carbon layer with the specific stated stabilizing function.
arguments.support_span: The ITO based conductive film 31 is printed with silver conductor lay 32. Then, a carbon layer 33, an insulation layer 34 and an adhesive layer 35 are coated sequentially on the printed silver conductor layer 32 as shown in FIG. 5.

arguments.assertion: The Examiner's prima facie obviousness finding relies on combining teachings to arrive at a carbon layer overlying the silver conductor; however, the specification shows alternative layer orders and explicitly ties the carbon layer to stabilization against silver ion dissociation in variable temperature and humidity environments, a specific technical effect not taught or suggested in the Examiner's characterization of the cited reference.
arguments.support_span: That is, the printed silver conductor layer 32 is on top of the ITO based conductive film 31, the carbon layer 33 is on top of the printed silver conductor layer 32, the insulation layer 34 is on top of the carbon layer 33, and the adhesive layer 35 is on top of the insulation layer 34.

arguments.assertion: Applicant will file corrected replacement drawing sheets that show the lower electrodes referenced in the specification and will remove bracketed reference numerals as required by 37 CFR 1.84 and 1.121(d).
arguments.support_span: The drawings are objected to as failing to comply with 37 CFR 1.84(p)(5) because they do not include the following reference sign(s) mentioned in the description: page 4, lines 16-20 recites that “The lower board 20 provides a layer of lower conductive film 21 made of Indium Tin Oxide (ITO) and a pair of lower electrodes 12, 14." Lower electrodes 12 and 14 are not shown on lower conductive film 21 of Fig. 4.

arguments.assertion: Applicant acknowledges the examiner's note that a certified copy of the Taiwanese priority application is required and will file the certified copy to perfect the claimed foreign priority.
arguments.support_span: It is noted, however, that applicant has not filed a certified copy of the Taiwanese application as required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b).

arguments.assertion: Applicant will amend the abstract to conform to MPEP § 608.01(b) and the examiner's guidance to avoid repetition of the title and to provide a single-paragraph narrative of appropriate length.
arguments.support_span: The abstract of the disclosure is objected to because it repeats information given in the title (input device for a man-machine interface). Correction is required. See MPEP § 608.01(b).

response.notes: Amendments to independent claims 1 and 6 add a functional limitation supported by the specification to distinguish the cited art as characterized in the Office action. Applicant will submit corrected drawings (replacement sheets), the certified foreign priority document, and a revised abstract in the reply per the examiner's instructions. Further amendments or evidence may be presented after review of the cited reference texts if needed.

edits.new_text: 1. A personal reminder digital voice recorder comprising: a) a battery operated audio microchip system for recording, storing and reproducing a single personal audio recording on each of a plurality of channels; b) an individual playback button assigned to each of the plurality of channels; c) an LED corresponding to each of the channels, each LED having a means to turn the LED on when the channel has an active message recorded; d) a means to turn each LED off when a corresponding channel has a message that is inactive; and e) wherein each playback button is assigned to a different person.

13. A personal digital recording device comprising a plurality of recording/playback channels wherein there is a playback button operating the playback for each of the channels on the device and there is a light corresponding to each playback button to indicate when the channel has an active message, wherein each playback button is assigned to a different person.

arguments.assertion: The cited prior art (MMR as characterized in the Office action) does not teach or disclose that each playback button is assigned to a different person, a limitation added to claims 1 and 13 and relied upon to distinguish the claimed device from the cited product descriptions and figures.
arguments.support_span: The different playback buttons can be assigned to different people, events, ideas and the like and by engaging or disengaging the corresponding LED lights one can keep track simply of short personal messages

arguments.assertion: The added limitation (each playback button assigned to a different person) is supported in the specification and is a structural/functional feature present in the embodiments, and thus is a proper narrowing amendment to distinguish over the MMR disclosures relied upon by the examiner.
arguments.support_span: The different playback buttons can be assigned to different people, events, ideas and the like and by engaging or disengaging the corresponding LED lights one can keep track simply of short personal messages

arguments.assertion: Claims 10 and 12 recite LED color-related features and the examiner's obviousness finding rests on taking official notice of general LED color options; applicant respectfully submits that the combination and specific use of color indications for message recipient or priority as described in the specification is not shown or suggested in the applied MMR reference as characterized by the Office action.
arguments.support_span: In one embodiment the LED light corresponding to a single channel can be lit as different colors. Thus, it could light one color indicating a new message and another color indicating a message still recorded on a channel but already listened to. Colors could also indicate who left the message or used to indicate the priority for the message (for example green for low priority and red for high priority).

arguments.assertion: The examiner relies on Pawlowski for a single-button interface selectable among many channels; applicant's claim 14 combines the single-playback-button concept with the per-channel LED indicators and the claimed combination is not shown in the MMR as characterized, and the Office action does not identify where Pawlowski teaches the claimed LED-per-channel indicator in combination with the specific features of MMR.
arguments.support_span: The present invention relates to a personal digital voice recorder with a plurality of channels and having a visual LED light indicator for each channel indicating if there is an active message on that channel.

arguments.assertion: Applicant asserts that the Office action's characterization of the cited non-patent product documentation (TERS/CTO) is taken from secondary sources and the examiner has not provided the full reference documents in the record; applicant requests that any findings of anticipation be made only if the examiner provides copies of the relied-upon non-patent references or otherwise makes the underlying evidence of disclosure of each specific claimed limitation of record.
arguments.support_span: A copy of this reference is not being furnished with this Office action. (See MPEP 707.05(a).)

arguments.assertion: Applicant will timely submit corrected replacement drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d) to resolve the examiner's drawing objections and will amend the drawings to add the missing reference signs and remove the extraneous figure reference as required.
arguments.support_span: Corrected drawing sheets in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(d), or amendment to the specification to add the reference character(s) in the description in compliance with 37 CFR 1.121(b) are required in reply to the Office action to avoid abandonment of the application.

response.notes: Applicant amends claims 1 and 13 to add a limitation supported by the specification to distinguish the claimed invention from the cited Multi Message Recorder characterizations. Applicant will submit replacement drawing sheets per 37 CFR 1.121(d) to address the drawing objections, and requests consideration of the above arguments. Further prosecution is respectfully requested.

A vacuum accelerator assist module connected to the carburetor having an intake chamber and a fuel metering chamber, comprising: a first housing half and a second housing half, each said housing half including a cavity; a diaphragm being retained between said first and second housing halves, said diaphragm creating the first chamber and the second chamber; and a spring for biasing said diaphragm into the second chamber, wherein, the first chamber communicating with the intake chamber of the carburetor, the second chamber communicating with the fuel metering chamber of the carburetor.
The vacuum accelerator assist module for a carburetor of claim 14 wherein: said spring being a compression spring.

arguments.assertion: The antecedent-basis deficiency noted by the examiner for claim 19 has been corrected by amending claim 19 to depend from claim 14 so that 'said spring' has proper antecedent basis.

arguments.support_span: Claims 1-20 would be allowable if (A) rewritten or amended to overcome the rejection under 35 U.S.C. 112, 2nd paragraph, set forth in this Office action, and (B) the following changes were made to the claims: (a) the word “for” on the first line of claims 1, 8, and 14 must be changed to --connected to--, (b) the phrase --having an intake chamber and a fuel metering chamber-- must be inserted immediately after the word “carburetor” on the first line of claims 1, 8, and 14, (c) the phrases "an intake chamber" and "a fuel metering chamber" in the last paragraph of claims 1, 8, and 14 must be changed to --the intake chamber-- and --the fuel metering chamber--, respectively,

arguments.support_span: The peripheral flange 18 of each housing half 10 preferably includes ae plurality of integral snap clips 34 extending therefrom and a plurality of snap cavities 36 formed therein for attaching the two housing halves 10 to each other and retaining the diaphragm 12...A spring retainer 28 includes a base 30 and a spring pin 32.

response.notes: Applicant has amended independent claims 1, 8, and 14 and claim 19 to address the examiner's 112(b) and formality suggestions. Applicant believes the amendments are supported by the specification and respectfully requests withdrawal of the 112(b) rejection as to claims 19-20 and consideration of the amended claims in view of the prior art rejections; applicant is available for an interview to discuss claim scope if the examiner desires.

edits.new_text: 343. A microarray comprising: an array of reservoirs, each reservoir comprising a reservoir body and a penetrating delivery member in fluid communication with the reservoir body, wherein the penetrating delivery member comprises a microneedle or other penetrating member configured to administer a therapeutic or diagnostic agent in tissue immediately adjacent to the penetrating delivery member and separate from other penetrating delivery members in the array.
344. The microarray of claim 343 further comprising biopsy mechanisms configured to separately extract, sample, or retain tissue or cells at the sites of administration.

346. The microarray of claim 343 wherein each of the reservoirs may be loaded with different substances and/or different microdose amounts of the substances, which can be released independently, and further comprising a controller configured to control release, the controller comprising a preprogrammed microprocessor, a receiver for remote control, or one or more sensors.
347. The microarray of claim 343 wherein one or more reservoirs comprise biodegradable polymeric matrices that release agent as a function of diffusion or degradation.

351. The microarray of claim 343 wherein the biopsy mechanisms comprise microneedles configured and arranged to retain a tissue sample upon retraction or to retain tissue in a chamber upon closing of a distal chamber element.

357. A microarray comprising an array of biopsy mechanisms, wherein each biopsy mechanism comprises a chamber having a proximal end and a distal end, and the distal end is configured with a cutting edge or closing member to separately extract tissue or cells from different sites within an individual.

358. The microarray of claim 357 further comprising assay or sensor elements associated with each biopsy mechanism, the assay or sensor elements being configured to separately sample or analyze the tissue or cells at the sites of extraction.

367. A method for delivering therapeutic or diagnostic agent to cells or tissue in an individual, and extracting, sampling or analyzing the tissue or cells comprising: providing the microarray of claim 343 comprising an array of reservoirs each having a penetrating delivery member configured to administer a microdose of therapeutic or diagnostic agent in tissue immediately adjacent to the penetrating delivery member and separate from other penetrating delivery members in the array; and using biopsy mechanisms of the microarray to separately extract, sample or analyze the tissue or cells at the sites of administration.
372. A method for extracting tissue or cells comprising providing the microarray of claim 357 and extracting cells or tissue at the site of each biopsy mechanism of the array.

arguments.assertion: The amended claims explicitly recite specific structures (e.g., microneedles, biopsy mechanisms, controllers comprising microprocessors, reservoir bodies, chambers with cutting edges) rather than purely functional “means for” language, and therefore do not invoke 35 U.S.C. 112(f).
arguments.support_span: The microchip devices and other devices of the present invention may also include a pump such as a microfluidic pump, an osmotic pump, or a microelectronic pump. ... each of the reservoirs of a microchip may be loaded with different substances and/or different microdose amounts of the substances, which can be released independently. ... In another variation, the devices include a biopsy mechanism for retaining tissue upon retrieval. ... the chambers may be configured to penetrate tissue, e.g., by employing a sharp or needle-like distal end.

arguments.assertion: The specification provides enabling disclosure of biopsy mechanisms and microneedle-based sampling including deployment, retention of tissue, and in vivo assays, such that a person of ordinary skill can make and use the claimed biopsy and sampling structures recited in the amended claims.
arguments.support_span: In some variations, the devices obtain or "biopsy" a sample of the target tissue at the time of implantation, upon removal or some time therebetween. ... By "sample" it is meant a tissue specimen obtained from the human body. ... The devices may obtain samples using any type of biopsy mechanism. In one variation, as shown in FIG. 4B, device (400) has a biopsy mechanism that causes the distal end (402) of the chambers (404) to move from an open position (FIG. 4A) to a closed position (FIG. 4B). Such a biopsy mechanism may include hinges, springs, shape memory elements, wires, or combinations thereof.

arguments.assertion: The examiner's indefiniteness objection to language such as 'may' and 'optionally' is addressed by the current amendments which present affirmative structural recitations (e.g., reservoirs comprising biodegradable polymeric matrices and a controller comprising a microprocessor or sensors) and thus provide definite scope and patentable weight to those limitations.
arguments.support_span: When the device includes a plurality of chambers, each reservoir may deliver the same substance or different substances. ... The microchip devices ... each of the reservoirs of a microchip may be loaded with different substances and/or different microdose amounts of the substances, which can be released independently. ... The devices may also include one or more sensors capable of sensing one or more parameters of the target tissue. The devices may include a memory component to store parameter or assay data, which can be downloaded after retrieval, or be configured to communicate the data outside the body.

arguments.assertion: Claims have been amended to include specific combination of structural features (for example: reservoirs each with penetrating microneedle delivery members in an array combined with biopsy mechanisms as recited) supported by the specification; to the extent the examiner finds Eppstein anticipates generalized features, the amended claims narrow to structural combinations and deployment/retention biopsy functionality that are not shown or taught in the examiner's characterization of Eppstein in the record.
arguments.support_span: When provided in a matrix, the substance may be homogeneously or heterogeneously distributed within the matrix. ... The devices may be configured for any route of delivery. For example, they may be implanted, ingested, or topically applied. ... In some variations, the devices include a biopsy mechanism for retaining tissue upon retrieval. In other variations, the devices include an assay component capable of evaluating samples or the general behavior of a substance in vivo, and preferably in real time.

arguments.assertion: With the amendments the claimed biopsy mechanisms and microneedle sampling features are drawn directly to embodiments described in the specification (including examples and figures); while the examiner relies on Jung for biopsy by microneedles, the amended claims require specific chamber/closure biopsy structures and reservoir-plus-penetrating-member combinations taught in this specification.
arguments.support_span: The devices may obtain samples using any type of biopsy mechanism. In one variation, as shown in FIG. 4B, device (400) has a biopsy mechanism that causes the distal end (402) of the chambers (404) to move from an open position (FIG. 4A) to a closed position (FIG. 4B). ... The chambers may be configured to penetrate tissue, e.g., by employing a sharp or needle-like distal end.

response.notes: Applicant submits the amended claims to (1) supply definite structural language to address the examiner's 35 U.S.C. 112(f) concern and to resolve the informalities noted (capitalization/punctuation issues will be corrected formally in the amendment transmittal), and (2) narrow the claims to structural embodiments supported by the specification to address the examiner's enablement/indefiniteness and prior-art rejections. Applicant requests withdrawal of the 35 U.S.C. 112(f) treatment for the amended claim limitations in view of the explicit structural recitations. Applicant is available to interview the examiner to expedite resolution.

edits.new_text: 20. A method of forming a lesion in the tissue of a left atrium comprising: advancing a first tissue-affecting device into the left atrium through a puncture in a left atrial appendage, wherein the first tissue-affecting device is positioned against the atrial wall; advancing a second tissue-affecting device to an external atrial wall, wherein the second tissue-affecting device is positioned against the external atrial wall opposite the first tissue-affecting device; positioning the first and second tissue-affecting devices such that ablation energy may pass between them; operating the first and second tissue-affecting devices simultaneously such that a lesion is formed in the atrial wall at least partially therebetween; and isolating the left atrial appendage.

arguments.assertion: The Examiner required an election and the applicant affirms election of the method claims (claims 11-24) as the elected invention for continued examination (in-person telephone provisional election made January 9, 2014); applicant therefore confirms prosecution should continue on claims 11-24 as elected, without traverse.
arguments.support_span: During a telephone conversation with Marcus Reeslund on January 9, 2014, a provisional election was made without traverse to prosecute invention II, claims 11-24. Affirmation of this election must be made by applicant in replying to this Office action.

arguments.assertion: Applicant has corrected the typographical error in claim 20 from 'therebtween' to 'therebetween' as required by the Office objection.

arguments.assertion: The specification discloses novel features and procedural details for using the left atrial appendage (LAA) as an access port, including use of the closure/stabilizing device with a looped snare, vacuum and dedicated working channel(s) for advancing piercing/access members and ablation arrays; these specific devices and steps present structural and procedural distinctions from the Examiner's characterization of Hooven and support patentable distinctions of the claimed methods.
arguments.support_span: [0037] Closure device (200) may comprise an elongate body (202), a handle portion (204) located at a proximal portion of the elongate body (202), an extension (205) located at a distal portion of the elongate body (202), and a distal looped closure assembly (206) distally coupled to the extension (205).

arguments.assertion: The specification specifically describes advancing an access/piercing member through the looped closure assembly /working channel and using vacuum and graspers to stabilize the LAA before puncture and device passage — procedural steps and stabilizing components that are set out in the claims and distinguish over what is characterized in the Office action.

arguments.assertion: Claim 17(verification), claim 18 (electrical impedance tomography) and claim 19 (thermal imaging) recite specific lesion verification/assessment steps and modalities that are described in the specification as post-ablation verification techniques and are not shown in the Office action to be taught by the single cited reference; the specification expressly lists electrical impedance tomography and thermal imaging among verification modalities.
arguments.support_span: [0058] ... verifying and assessing the lesion using fluoroscopic, electrical impedance, and thermal imaging techniques.

response.notes: Applicant affirms the provisional election of the method claims (claims 11-24) for continued examination (per phone election Jan 9, 2014). Applicant has amended claim 20 solely to correct the typographical error noted by the Office. Applicant presents arguments and requests that the Examiner consider the specification passages cited above in reassessing the 35 U.S.C. 102 and 103 rejections; for the Examiner's asserted combinations relying on references not fully of record in the Office action, applicant requests that Examiner point to the exact passages in those references relied upon to establish the combination and motivation to combine so that applicant may respond fully.

edits.new_text: 1. A blade comprising: an aerodynamic blade body comprising a leading edge and a trailing edge; at least one flexible adaptor component having a first side coupled to the trailing edge; and at least one separate and removable rigid acoustic segment attached to an opposing second side of the at least one flexible adapter component for mitigating noise during fluid flow over the blade.

15. A flexible trailing edge adapter component for a wind blade; the trailing edge adapter component comprising: a first side portion shaped for attachment to a truncated airfoil trailing edge of the wind blade; and a second side portion shaped for attachment of a plurality of separate and removable rigid acoustic segments.

arguments.assertion: The examiner's combination relies on modifying Standish's integral or non-separable trailing-edge noise-attenuating shape by substituting van der Bos' attached segments, but neither cited reference teaches or suggests that the noise-attenuating component is a separate and removable rigid acoustic segment attached to the adapter component as recited in the amended claim.
arguments.support_span: Standish further discloses providing the trailing edge assembly with a noise attenuating shape (Figures 7, 10 and 12) however the noise attenuating features are not separate components and therefore Standish does not explicitly disclose at least one rigid acoustic segment attached to an opposing second side of the at least one flexible adapter component for mitigating noise during fluid flow over the blade.

arguments.assertion: The specification describes and supports separate and removable rigid acoustic segments attached to the adapter component and the benefits of replacement/repair and mechanical decoupling, which distinguishes the claimed separate-and-removable segments from an integral molded noise-attenuating trailing-edge shape.
arguments.support_span: Using mechanical fasteners enables easy replacement or repair of the flexible adaptor components. Furthermore, reductions in stressed concentrations at mechanical attachment points allow use of longer trailing edge segments and enable reduced part count or fewer trailing edge segments on each blade.

arguments.assertion: The examiner's conclusion that it would have been obvious to select a material within the claimed Young's modulus range from the general categories of rubber or plastic is a factual assertion about what a skilled artisan would select that is not supported by the cited references of record; the specification, however, does support the claimed modulus range as a disclosed embodiment.
arguments.support_span: In one embodiment, the at least one flexible adapter component 12 comprises a flexible material with a young's modulus ranging from about 0.7 MPa to about 3500MPa. In a more specific embodiment, the flexible material of the adapter component 12 may have a young's modulus ranging from about 7 MPa to about 500MPa.

arguments.assertion: The examiner's combination reasoning (that van der Bos' attachment 'would work equally as well' on Standish) is a conclusory hindsight-style assertion about obvious interchangeability that does not address design, function, or motivation differences between a one-piece noise-attenuating trailing edge and a removable rigid segment attached to an adapter component.
arguments.support_span: Since both Standish and van der Bos discloses wind turbine blades having trailing edge assemblies wherein noise attenuating components are attached and it is clear that the attachment method of van der Bos would work equally as well as the method disclosed by Standish and the end result would be fundamentally the same, it would have been obvious at the time the invention was made one of ordinary kill in the art to modify the trailing edge assembly of Standish, with the teachings of van der Bos, by providing the separate and removable noise attenuating component for the purpose of providing a component that can be quickly and efficiently attached and removed from the trailing edge.

response.notes: Amendments add 'separate and removable' to independent claim 1 and claim 15 to distinguish from Standish's integral noise-attenuating shapes as characterized by the examiner. Applicant preserves remaining claims; further prosecution may present additional evidence or amendments if necessary.

The operating device according to claim 1, comprising a jacket member that covers the plurality of detection units.

The operating device according to claim 2, characterized in that the jacket member is capable of rotating around the circumference of the casing at least within the range in which the plurality of detection units are arranged.
The operating device according to claim 2, characterized in that an input unit for inputting the input is provided on the jacket member.

edits.new_text: 1. arguments.assertion: Claim 1 has been amended to recite a ring retainer made of an elastic spring material with a head and foot that engages a groove in the tubular housing to apply a retained loading force to the weld ring/O-ring interface; this particular ring-retainer limitation is disclosed in the specification and was not specifically relied upon in the Examiner's rejection as recited in the Office action against the original claim 1.

arguments.support_span: Claims 6-18 and 23-25 are objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.

edits.new_text: 1. A laser projection system, comprising: a laser module having at least a laser device to emit a single wavelength laser beam; a red fluorescent member excited by the laser beam from the laser module to emit a red beam; a green fluorescent member excited by the laser beam from the laser module to emit a green beam; a blue fluorescent member excited by the laser beam from the laser module to emit a blue beam; a first collimator on a path of the red beam from the red fluorescent member to collimate the red beam; a second collimator on a path of the green beam from the green fluorescent member to collimate the green beam; a third collimator on a path of the blue beam from the blue fluorescent member to collimate the blue beam; a prism receiving the collimated beams from the first collimator, the second collimator, and the third collimator to reflect the red beam, the green beam, and the blue beam respectively; and a scanning optical system projecting the red beam, the green beam, and the blue beam from the prism onto an image surface to form an image.
2. The laser projection system as defined in claim 1, further comprising a fourth collimator between the laser module and the fluorescent members to collimate the laser beam from the laser module.

4. The laser projection system as defined in claim 1, further comprising a first dichroic mirror between the fluorescent members and the prism to pass the red beam therethrough and reflect the green beam and the blue beam.

5. The laser projection system as defined in claim 1, further comprising a second dichroic mirror between the fluorescent members and the prism to pass the blue beam therethrough and reflect the green beam.
6. The laser projection system as defined in claim 1, further comprising a third mirror between the blue fluorescent member and the prism to reflect the blue beam.

arguments.assertion: The amendments replace ambiguous uses of 'lens' with specific terms used in the specification (e.g., 'scanning optical system', 'first dichroic mirror', 'second dichroic mirror', 'third mirror'), resolving the indefinite use of 'lens' by aligning claim language with the disclosure.

arguments.support_span: [0007] As shown in FIG. 1, a laser projection system of the preferred embodiment of the present invention includes a laser module 10, ... a red fluorescent member 30-1, a green fluorescent member 30-2, and a blue fluorescent member 30-3, ... a first collimator 40-1, a second collimator 40-2, and a third collimator 40-3, ... a prism 60, ... and a scan system lens 80.

arguments.assertion: Amendments replacing generic 'lens' language with 'first dichroic mirror', 'second dichroic mirror', and 'third mirror' more precisely claim the separation unit arrangement described in the specification and distinguish over the examiner's generalized combination of references.
arguments.support_span: [0010] The red, green, and blue beams emit to the first, second, and third collimators 40-1, 40-2, and 40-3 respectively to be collimated again ... edits.new_text: 11. A system for generating a personalized script, comprising: a computer system comprising a processor and a non-transitory computer-readable memory storing program code; a template stored in the memory including an established format having a generic framework including generic data components; said generic data components comprise at least one of video, audio, image, graphics and text; said program code, when executed by the processor, implements functional scripts for defining how said generic data components are to be combined with personalized data components; said personalized data components comprise at least one of video, audio, image, graphics and text; said program code merges said personalized data components for insertion of said personalized data components into said template; and, said program code includes commands for modifying insertion times and insertion locations of said personalized data components for said merging with said template thereby creating said personalized script.

arguments.assertion: Amendment adds concrete physical hardware (a computer system with a processor and non-transitory memory) and program code that, when executed, implements the claimed functional scripts, thereby reciting a statutory machine rather than abstract software per se.
arguments.support_span: The electronic capturing device can be interfaced to a central computer having a keyboard (not shown), the computer can be responsible for the various editing and control features necessary to carry out personalization associated with producing a final electronic record

arguments.assertion: The examiner's cited passages do not establish that the cited reference teaches generation of dynamic scripts that integrate personalized data components into a generic framework for asynchronous video creation as claimed, including use of script variables that alter template timing/format based on metadata for real-time synthesis; the specification explicitly describes dynamic scripting and execution by a synthesis tool such as AviSynth or Adobe After Effects enabling real-time generation.
arguments.support_span: The present disclosure proposes creating personalized videos using dynamic scripts that are executed by a video synthesis tool such as AviSynth@ or Adobe After Effects@ .

arguments.assertion: Combination with Ramamurthy, as applied by the examiner, does not supply a factual showing that Ramamurthy teaches generating runtime scripts that alter template temporal properties as functions of personalized metadata to produce an asynchronous personalized script in real time as claimed; the specification describes precisely these features (script generation from metadata and real-time execution).
arguments.support_span: Using variables that are functions of a given set of metadata a corresponding personalized script can integrate the various timings of the template video and the personalized components into a continuous stream.

response.notes: Applicant files the above amendment to claim 11 to address the 35 U.S.C. 101 rejection by reciting a concrete computer system and program code. Applicant submits the accompanying arguments distinguishing the prior art rejections and provides support from the specification for claimed features. edits.new_text: 1. The management apparatus according to claim 4, wherein the copy pair setting unit: displays a copy pair setting screen for designating the respective virtual volumes which are the copy source and the copy destination constituting the copy pair, and the copy pair setting policy; and switches a part or whole of each of the logical volumes, which are associated with the respective virtual volumes designated as the copy source and the copy destination of the copy pair on the copy pair setting screen, to an appropriate logical volume as necessary in accordance with the copy pair setting policy designated by using the copy pair setting screen.

edits.new_text: An apparatus to use relatively rigid sheet materials, to make boxes, the apparatus comprising loading means for loading, according to a desired order, one or more substantially flat reinforcement elements; and gripping means movable between a first gripping position in which the gripping means cooperates with said loading means for picking up one or more of said reinforcement elements, and a second positioning condition, in which the gripping means positions said reinforcement elements on said sheet while the sheet is in a substantially flat, unfolded condition upstream of any folding station, according to a predetermined positioning pattern which includes at least units formed by three reinforcement elements disposed adjacent along respective edges of the plane of the sheet according to a right-angled travel, so that, by actuating a coordinated folding of lips of the sheet in order to form the box, the reciprocal positioning of the reinforcement elements is defined, so as to form substantially a single corner reinforcement element in which the reinforcement elements are disposed in contact with each other along said edges and lie on a coordinated triad of different Cartesian planes.

A method for forming boxes using relatively rigid sheet materials, the method comprising: feeding said sheet along a direction of movement, on which sheet specific cutting and pre-creasing workings have been made along the direction, so as to define relative lips and fold lines on the sheet; at least a positioning step on the sheet, in correspondence at least to angles identified by said junction of said fold lines, of substantially flat reinforcement elements according to a predetermined positioning pattern which includes at least units formed by three reinforcement elements disposed adjacent along respective edges on the plane of the sheet according to a right-angled travel mating with the respective angle in correspondence to which the reinforcement elements are positioned, wherein the positioning step is performed while the sheet is in a substantially flat, unfolded condition upstream of any folding station; and a coordinated folding step of the lips of the sheet to form the box, so as to define the reciprocal positioning of the reinforcement elements, to form substantially a single corner reinforcement element in which the reinforcement elements are disposed in contact with each other along said respective edges and lie on a coordinated triad of different Cartesian planes.

arguments.assertion: The phrases in question lacked antecedent words are corrected by explicit antecedent phrasing and by specifying that positioning occurs while the sheet is 'in a substantially flat, unfolded condition upstream of any folding station', which is supported by the specification disclosure that the unit operates on the sheet in a substantially flat condition upstream of folding.
arguments.support_span: Advantageously, the unit according to the present invention is applied downstream of units or stations for cutting and/or pre-creasing the sheet, and upstream of units and/or stations for folding the sheets, with respect to the direction of feed of the sheet. In this way, the working unit according to the present invention is suitable to operate on the cardboard sheet in a substantially flat condition, that is, before its conformation into a box.

arguments.assertion: Liebeskind as characterized by the Examiner (machine for adding reinforcements) is not shown to teach placing multiple substantially-flat reinforcement elements on the sheet while the sheet is still flat so that subsequent folding converts adjacent flat elements into a single corner reinforcement element occupying three perpendicular planes; the specification expressly teaches positioning flat elements on the flat blank upstream of folding to achieve that result.
arguments.support_span: According to the present invention, the positioning pattern includes at least units formed by three reinforcement elements disposed adjacent along respective edges on the plane of the sheet according to a right-angled travel, so that, by actuating a coordinated folding of lips of the sheet in order to form the box, the reciprocal positioning of the reinforcement elements is defined to substantially form a single corner reinforcement element in which the reinforcement elements are disposed in contact with each other along the respective edges and lie on a coordinated triad of different and reciprocally perpendicular Cartesian planes.

arguments.assertion: While the Examiner takes official notice that optical viewing means are generally known, the specification provides specific integrated control/marker/viewing functionality (images transmitted to a command and control unit that recognizes sheet format and coordinates marking) — a particular combination and control flow not shown or argued to be taught in the cited art as a whole.

edits.new_text: 1. A method for correlating a plurality of messages conforming to different protocols and associated with a common communication call in a communication network, comprising the steps of: extracting an information from a message; extracting a protocol specific identifier to identify the protocol to which the message conforms, such that all the messages conforming to the same protocol have the same protocol specific identifier; forming a plurality of protocol specific queues, such that messages having same protocol specific identifier are in same queue; forming a correlation identifier ("correlation ID") using the information extracted from the message and the protocol specific identifier of the message, such that the messages associated with the same communication call have same correlation ID; and forming a call specific queue comprising of messages extracted from the plurality of protocol specific queues associated with the same common communication call and having same correlation ID, wherein the "protocols" are telecom or messaging protocols and the "common communication call" is a communication call or business entity as described in the specification.
2. The method according to claim 1, further comprising the processing of messages from the call specific queue with first-in-first-out (FIFO) criterion.

4. The method according to claim 1, wherein the protocols are telecom and messaging protocols from a list including a SIP, a HTTP, a MGCP, a Diameter, a CAP, a MAP, an INAP, a SMTP, a SMPP protocols or a combination thereof, as exemplified in the specification.

arguments.assertion: The specification provides enabling disclosure of using protocol-specific identifiers, forming protocol-specific queues, forming a correlation identifier from extracted information and protocol-specific identifier, and storing the correlation ID in memory; a person skilled in the art can implement the claimed method without undue experimentation.

[0038] The correlation ID may include a plurality of call context specific identifiers such as message source identifier, destination identifier etc. The correlation ID is saved in a memory of a system where the method 100 is applied.

arguments.assertion: The amendments identify and define abbreviations and key terms in the claims (for example, defining 'correlation ID' as 'correlation identifier ("correlation ID")', specifying "protocols" are telecom or messaging protocols, and clarifying FIFO), thereby resolving the examiner's indefiniteness concerns under 35 U.S.C. 112(b).

arguments.assertion: The examiner's characterization of the cited references does not establish that the combination renders the claimed invention obvious because the present specification uniquely teaches in-memory mapping of protocol-specific identifiers to a correlation ID and forming call-specific queues to avoid head-of-line blocking, features not shown by the examiner's characterizations of Hammer and Martin.

arguments.assertion: Terms the examiner identified as indefinite (for example 'disengaged state', 'slipping engagement state', 'direct engagement state', 'transfer torque capacity', and how second engagement device transition is detected) are expressly defined and described in the specification and thus are definite to a person skilled in the art.

it may be determined that the second engagement device has transitioned from the direct engagement state to the slipping engagement state on the basis of a fact that the rotational speed difference across the second engagement device has become equal to or more than a predetermined value.

edits.new_text: 1. A system for estimating thrust from an engine, comprising: a vehicle having a propulsion device that is capable of producing thrust, said propulsion device is attached by at least one mounting structure; at least one strain gauge mounted on said mounting structure, said strain gauge for producing a signal indicative of stress; at least one accelerometer mounted on one of said propulsion device or vehicle, said accelerometer producing a signal indicative of acceleration; and at least one processor in communication with said strain gauge and accelerometer for estimating thrust from strain gauge signals and said acceleration signals.
2. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 1, wherein the processor estimates a transient portion of thrust by converting accelerometer signals to measured acceleration.
3. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 2, wherein a transient portion of thrust is estimated by multiplying a mass by measured acceleration.

8. A system for estimating thrust from an engine, comprising: a vehicle having an engine capable of producing thrust, said engine attached by at least one mounting member; at least one strain gauge mounted on said engine mount, said strain gauge for producing a signal indicative of stress; at least one accelerometer mounted on said vehicle, said accelerometer producing a signal indicative of acceleration; and at least one processor in communication with said strain gauge and said accelerometer for estimating thrust from the strain gauge signals and the acceleration signals according to an algorithm.
9. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 8, wherein said algorithm adds steady state measurements and transient measurements to calculate total thrust.
10. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 9, wherein the algorithm estimates the transient portion of thrust from accelerometer signals.
11. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 10, wherein the algorithm estimates the transient portion of thrust by multiplying mass by measured acceleration.
12. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 9, wherein the algorithm estimates the steady state portion of thrust from the strain gauge signals.
13. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 12, wherein said algorithm estimates the steady state portion of thrust from the strain gauge signals and stiffness of said engine mount.
14. The system for estimating thrust as set forth in claim 12, wherein said estimate of steady state thrust uses an estimate of drag force on said vehicle.

arguments.assertion: The specification expressly discloses a processor and a code segment used to estimate thrust from strain gauge and accelerometer signals, supporting the claimed processor-based estimators and algorithmic estimation.
arguments.support_span: In one embodiment the algorithm 23 is in the form of a code segment 19 containing instructions 21 to estimate thrust from strain gage signals and acceleration signals. In one embodiment at least one processor 17 is in communication with the strain gauge 13 and accelerometer 15 for executing instructions 21 to estimate thrust from strain gauge signals and acceleration signals.

arguments.assertion: The specification provides structural and positional disclosure of strain gauges and accelerometers mounted to engine mounts, propulsion device and vehicle body, supporting the claim elements reciting those sensors.
arguments.support_span: At least one strain gauge is mounted on the engine mount 44. ... At least one accelerometer 15 for producing a signal indicative of acceleration is mounted on the vehicle 50. One example of a suitable accelerometer is a 3-axis MEMS accelerometer. In one embodiment the accelerometer 15 is located in an engine 10. ... In one embodiment the accelerometer 15 is mounted to the body of the vehicle 50.

arguments.support_span: In one embodiment the algorithm 23 estimates a transient portion of thrust by converting accelerometer signals measured acceleration. In one embodiment, a transient portion of thrust it is estimated by multiplying a mass by measured acceleration.

arguments.assertion: The specification discloses combining steady-state (strain-based) and transient (accel-based) measurements and that steady-state estimates may use strain gauge signals, mount stiffness, and drag estimates.

arguments.support_span: An algorithm combines steady-state and transient measurements to determine an estimation of thrust from an engine. By adding the steady-state portion and transient portion of thrust the algorithm is able to estimate thrust.

arguments.assertion: Applicant will file replacement drawings showing the sensors on the engine mount/vehicle body to cure the drawing objection under 37 C.F.R. 1.83(a), rather than canceling sensor limitations from the claims.

edits.new_text: An article of manufacture comprising a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having computer program code embodied therein, wherein the computer program code when executed in at least one processing device causes at least one processing device to perform a method comprising steps of: receiving content from a plurality of sources; generating positional information for the sources wherein the positional information indicates for each of the sources its current position in a set of possible positions relative to other ones of the sources; generating multiple content streams comprising respective portions of the content received from respective ones of the sources based at least in part on the positional information and a mapping between the content streams and the sources; transmitting the content streams with their associated positional information over a network; detecting a change in position of at least a given one of the sources relative to other ones of the sources; responsive to the change in position of the given source, altering the mapping between the multiple content streams and the sources; and repeating at least a subset of the steps utilizing the altered mapping; wherein the steps are implemented in at least one processing device comprising a processor coupled to a memory.

An article of manufacture comprising a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium having computer program code embodied therein, wherein the computer program code when executed in at least one processing device causes at least one processing device to perform the method of claim 17.

arguments.support_span: A claim drawn to a computer-readable storage medium (also called machine readable medium and other such variations) typically covers forms of non-transitory tangible media (or non-transitory media) and transitory propagating signals per se...

arguments.assertion: The pending independent claims require altering the mapping between content streams and sources responsive to detection of a change in position and then repeating at least a subset of the steps (including generating and transmitting content streams) utilizing the altered mapping; this specific sequence and repetition by the media control center and video server as recited is supported by the specification and is a required element of the claims.

edits.new_text: 1. A mobile terminal, comprising: a touchscreen configured to sense touch inputs and comprising a fingerprint sensor integrated with the touchscreen; and a controller configured to determine whether a touch input is an input using a finger of a user and, responsive to determining that the touch input is an input using the user's finger and that a function associated with the touch input requires authentication, to request from the fingerprint sensor a fingerprint image corresponding only to touch sensors contacted by the user's finger and to provide a prescribed user interface for authentication based on the requested fingerprint image, the prescribed user interface for authentication when the touch input is an input using a user's finger being different than a user interface for authentication when the touch input is not an input using a user's finger.

15. A method for controlling a mobile terminal, comprising: receiving touch input applied to a touchscreen having an integrated fingerprint sensor; processing the touch input to determine whether the touch input is an input using a finger of a user; and, responsive to determining that the touch input is an input using the user's finger and that a function associated with the touch input requires authentication, requesting from the fingerprint sensor a fingerprint image corresponding only to touch sensors contacted by the user's finger and providing a user interface for authentication based on the requested fingerprint image, wherein the user interface for authentication when the touch input is an input using the user's finger is different than a user interface necessary for authentication when the touch input is not an input using a user's finger.

arguments.assertion: The examiner's primary combination relies on Kennedy to supply a general ability to distinguish finger versus pen input, but the specification and the amended claims require that the controller, upon determining a finger input and that authentication is needed, request a fingerprint image corresponding only to touch sensors contacted by the user's finger (i.e., selective-region fingerprint acquisition), which is not taught by the cited combination as asserted by the examiner.
arguments.support_span: The touch IC 151b can acquire a fingerprint image of a region with which the user's finger comes into contact on the touchscreen 151 (S207). The touch IC 151a can obtain a fingerprint image of the user through an operation of scanning only a region of the touchscreen 151, which comes into contact with the user's finger, only at the request of the application processor 181a, as described above, rather than acquiring the fingerprint image whenever touch input by the user's finger is received.

arguments.assertion: Funahashi as characterized in the Office action does show fingerprint registration/authentication and separate UI types, but does not disclose the particular combination limitation requiring an integrated fingerprint sensor to be queried for a fingerprint image limited to the touched touch-sensor region only when both (a) a finger input is detected and (b) the function requires authentication; that specific selective-request behavior is supported by the present specification and narrows the claims over the cited art.
arguments.support_span: Accordingly, the touch IC 151b transmits the acquired fingerprint image to the application processor 181a (S209, Fingerprint Image Report). The application processor 181a can perform fingerprint authentication by comparing the fingerprint image received from the touch IC 151b with pre-stored fingerprint information of the user (S211). The touch IC 151a can obtain a fingerprint image of the user through an operation of scanning only a region of the touchscreen 151, which comes into contact with the user's finger, only at the request of the application processor 181a, as described above, rather than acquiring the fingerprint image whenever touch input by the user's finger is received.

arguments.assertion: The amended method claim recites requesting the fingerprint image corresponding only to the touched sensors and providing a UI based on that requested image; the specification describes that the touch IC is requested to provide the fingerprint image when authentication is necessary and that the touch IC performs scanning of only the region contacted by the finger, supporting the amended steps.
arguments.support_span: The application processor 181a can request the touch IC 151b to provide the fingerprint information of the user (S205). The touch IC 151b can acquire a fingerprint image of a region with which the user's finger comes into contact on the touchscreen 151 (S207).

arguments.assertion: Dependent aspects regarding processing only the finger portion when other body parts also contact the touchscreen are separately disclosed in the specification and stand as additional features beyond the examiner's cited art combination; the spec explicitly teaches ignoring non-finger contacts while processing the finger contact normally.
arguments.support_span: When the touch input is recognized as touch input by a part of the body of the user other than the finger, the controller may be configured to process only touch input by the finger of the user as normal touch input. For example, handwriting input 50 may be applied by the user's finger F1 to the touchscreen 151 ... only the touch input by the user's finger F1 may be recognized as normal touch input and touch input by the remaining portion of the user's hand ... may be ignored without being processed as normal touch input.

response.notes: Amendments narrow independent device and method claims to recite the selective-region fingerprint-image request/scan limitation supported by the specification. Argument units point to the supporting specification passages showing claimed selective behavior which distinguishes over the examiner's cited combination as characterized in the Office action.

arguments.assertion: The Examiner has already determined that claims 10-18 are allowable under 35 U.S.C. 101.

edits.new_text: A superconducting magnet made from epitaxially deposited superconductor tapes, wherein the magnet is a toroidally-wound coil and a superconductor tape width is poloidally graded by varying the width of the epitaxial tapes as the tapes wrap around the torus so that, when used in the coil, the margin, defined as a ratio between the operating current and the critical current, is relatively constant throughout the coil.

arguments.assertion: The amended claim 1 recites poloidal grading by varying the epitaxial tape width as the tapes wrap around a torus, a specific construction and limitation that is supported by the specification and distinguishes from the examiner's characterization of the cited MIT reference.
arguments.support_span: For an HTS toroidal winding, grading can also be obtained by varying the widths of tapes as they wrap around the toroid, as shown in Figure 2. This approach is unique to YBCO 2nd generation tapes and similar tapes, such as ReBCO;

arguments.assertion: The examiner's anticipation argument relies on an assertion that MIT teaches the same limitation; however, the Office action does not provide a verbatim disclosure of poloidal grading in a toroidally-wound coil with the specific limitation 'as the tapes wrap around the torus' as recited in the amended claim.
arguments.support_span: Regarding claim 1, MIT teaches a superconducting magnet ... wherein a superconductor tape width is adjusted ... so that, when used in a magnet having a coil, the margin ... is relatively constant throughout the coil.

arguments.assertion: The obviousness combination asserted by the examiner (MIT + Young) fails to establish that a person of ordinary skill would have had reason to modify Young's toroidal/support structures with MIT's multi-width tape teachings to achieve the specific poloidal grading and its consequences recited in the claims.
arguments.support_span: In order to minimize the amount of superconductor used, the following approach is used: Grading of the tapes by varying the width of the tape as it varies poloidally along the torus.

arguments.assertion: Young (as relied on by the examiner) concerns structural support units and plates but the examiner has not shown that Young suggests the particular combination of one or more shells made from multiple shell sectors together with a plurality of radial plates connected mechanically or thermally for both load and thermal management as claimed.
arguments.support_span: Regarding claim 6, MIT teaches the superconducting magnet of claim 1, but is silent regarding comprising one or more shells made from multiple shell sectors, and a plurality of radial plates connected mechanically or thermally for load and thermal management.

arguments.assertion: The examiner's combination of Young and MIT does not identify or argue that Young teaches adjusting radial distances between strands in plates to reduce field peaking or adjusting plate thickness for minimal structure in the manner and context taught in the specification.
arguments.support_span: By adjusting the current distribution in the plates (such as, for example, by adjusting the location of the strands/cables in the plates), it is possible to minimize the field peaking, at the expense of reduced overall field

arguments.assertion: Kobayashi (as characterized by the examiner) is cited against claim 10, but the Office action does not show that Kobayashi discloses the combination of one-or-more shells that produce a 1/r field together with radial plates that provide currents required to maintain a near-constant magnetic field in the bore in the specific hybrid arrangement recited.
arguments.support_span: Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(1)/(a)(2) as being anticipated by Kobayashi (US 2010/0029487).

arguments.assertion: The specification describes a hybrid magnet in which shells produce a 1/R field and radial plates introduce currents to maintain a near-constant field, supporting the claimed hybrid configuration and its specific function; the examiner has not pointed to a passage in Kobayashi that discloses this hybrid functionality in the same manner.
arguments.support_span: An alternative approach is to use a hybrid magnet, using a shell winding, that establishes the 1/R toroidal field, in combinations with radial or near radial plates that generate the near constant toroidal field in the bore of the magnet.

response.notes: Amendment narrows claim 1 to explicitly recite toroidal winding and poloidal grading by varying tape width as the tape wraps around the torus, supported in the specification. Claim 5 cancelled as redundant with amended claim 1 and to address the examiner's anticipation finding. Arguments emphasize lack of demonstrated teaching or motivation in the applied references to arrive at the claimed specific combinations and limitations.

arguments.assertion: The examiner’s identification of Hayashi as disclosing the claimed layered PDLC+GHLC structure does not address multiple concrete structural features recited in the claims and described in the specification, e.g., the GHLC wall with dams creating separated liquid crystal areas and the specific adhesive-attached alignment-film arrangement on the dams; these are structural, not merely functional, limitations supported by the specification.

edits.new_text: 1. A method of controlling a memory module having memory components disposed thereon, the method comprising: outputting first and second memory read commands to the memory module at respective times; receiving first read data concurrently from a first plurality of the memory components via a first plurality of data paths, respectively, in response to the first memory read command; and receiving second read data concurrently from a second plurality of the memory components via a second plurality of data paths, respectively, in response to the second memory read command, the first plurality of the memory components including at least one memory component not included in the second plurality of the memory components and vice-versa, wherein at least one memory component of the memory module is an annealable memory component comprising integrated anneal circuitry, and wherein the method further comprises outputting, to the annealable memory component, a maintenance command that instructs the annealable memory component to execute an anneal operation that heats an integrated-circuit memory die of the annealable memory component to reverse operational degradation.

11. A memory control component comprising: control logic to output first and second memory read commands to a memory module at respective times, the memory module having memory components disposed thereon; and interface circuitry to receive (i) first read data concurrently from a first plurality of the memory components via a first plurality of data paths, respectively, in response to the first memory read command, and (ii) second read data concurrently from a second plurality of the memory components via a second plurality of data paths, respectively, in response to the second memory read command, the first plurality of the memory components including at least one memory component not included in the second plurality of the memory components and vice-versa, wherein at least one memory component of the memory module is an annealable memory component comprising integrated anneal circuitry, and wherein the control logic is further to output a maintenance command to the annealable memory component that instructs the annealable memory component to execute an anneal operation that heats an integrated-circuit memory die of the annealable memory component to reverse operational degradation.

20. A memory control component comprising: means for outputting first and second memory read commands to a memory module at respective times, the memory module having memory components disposed thereon; and means for receiving (i) first read data concurrently from a first plurality of the memory components via a first plurality of data paths, respectively, in response to the first memory read command, and (ii) second read data concurrently from a second plurality of the memory components via a second plurality of data paths, respectively, in response to the second memory read command, the first plurality of the memory components including at least one memory component not included in the second plurality of the memory components and vice-versa, wherein at least one of the memory components is an annealable memory component including integrated anneal circuitry, and wherein the means for outputting is further for outputting a maintenance command that instructs the annealable memory component to execute an anneal operation that heats an integrated-circuit memory die of the annealable memory component to reverse operational degradation.

arguments.assertion: The cited Lee reference, as characterized by the examiner, does not disclose that any memory component includes integrated anneal circuitry or that maintenance commands cause heating of an integrated-circuit memory die to reverse operational degradation (an anneal operation).
arguments.support_span: A system that performs in-situ annealing operations to extend the utility of use-degraded components is disclosed in various embodiments. ... the anneal circuitry includes three basic components ... a heating element ...; power-control circuitry ...; and interface circuitry to receive commands that may be applied to the power-control circuitry to execute an anneal operation

arguments.assertion: The amended claims introduce the specific feature that the maintenance command instructs execution of an anneal operation that heats a memory die; this feature is not shown in the examiner's factual statement as being taught by Lee (examiner's characterization focuses on concurrent reads, chip select behavior, and maintenance commands generally but does not establish heating/anneal).
arguments.support_span: As per claims 2 and 12, Lee teaches a method and memory control component further comprising outputting a maintenance command ... the maintenance command instructing the memory component to handle a particular operation concurrently with the pending memory operations, paragraph 46.

arguments.assertion: The examiner relies on Tsern to supply DIMM and page-table teachings; even if Tsern discloses DIMM or page-table use, the combination with Lee does not supply the anneal-specific heating limitation newly recited in claims 1, 11 and 20, so the proposed amendment provides a non-obvious distinguishing technical feature over the cited combination.
arguments.support_span: The anneal capability may be implemented by anneal circuitry integrated within an integrated-circuit memory die (on-die anneal circuitry), inside an integrated circuit package ... and/or formed separately from but disposed in proximity to an integrated-circuit memory die or package (in-system anneal circuitry).

arguments.assertion: Bhakta (per examiner) is said to disclose virtual pairing; however Bhakta (as characterized) does not address anneal operations that heat a memory die to reverse operational degradation, and thus cannot render obvious the amended claims' anneal-specific limitation.
arguments.support_span: In particular, a number of embodiments are presented in the context of an annealable memory subsystem formed by flash memory components ... a number of challenges are presented within an annealable memory subsystem ... managing the migration (or evacuation) of data from a memory device to be annealed to an alternate storage is a characteristic of a number of embodiments described below.

response.notes: Applicant amends the independent claims to recite anneal/annealable memory components and an anneal operation that heats an integrated-circuit memory die, relying on the specification support for in-situ annealing. Applicant also submits arguments that the cited prior art (as characterized in the Office action) does not disclose or render obvious the newly-added anneal-specific heating limitations. Applicant requests withdrawal of the 102/103 rejections to the extent they do not address the amended claims' anneal-specific subject matter; applicant is available to further amend or present evidence if the examiner cites prior art that specifically teaches heating an integrated-circuit memory die for anneal as claimed.

arguments.support_span: the mapping unit 102 operates to paraphrase one or more portions of patent claim elements or limitations, and map the paraphrase to a concept. In some embodiments, the paraphrased portion is a general idea derived from a claim that is implicit to the claim, but not explicitly stated in the claim.

arguments.assertion: The specification describes execution on computing devices, processors, memory and a database, demonstrating the claimed method is tied to a particular machine and transforms stored patent mappings and pools, satisfying Alice step two.
